mainTopic: The end of a discussion about protest (מחאה), followed by a new case: two people both claim a field as 'my ancestors'', and רבה and אביי argue whether מה לי לשקר works against witnesses.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case. If the land was held for only six years, the other side's sale of the land is the strongest possible מחאה. Then a new case begins. Two people each say a field came from their ancestors. One brings witnesses that it was his ancestors'. The other brings witnesses that he used it for the years of חזקה. רבה rules for the one in possession because of מה לו לשקר. אביי answers that this rule does not work against witnesses. The one in possession then changes his story: 'It was your ancestors', but I bought it from you.' This raises the question of טוען וחוזר וטוען, whether a person may adjust his claim. עולא says yes and the חכמי נהרדעא say no, and each side admits limits. אמימר sides with עולא, and that is the הלכה. A second case follows. One side has witnesses to his ancestors' ownership and to years of use, while the other has witnesses only to use. רב נחמן rules that the two testimonies about use cancel out, so the land goes to the ancestral owner. רבא objects that the witnesses were contradicted. רב נחמן begins his answer, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Six years: the sale itself is the strongest protest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier case. If only six years passed, the other party's sale of the land counts as the strongest possible מחאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it was only six years, there is no greater protest than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing the case it was discussing just before this line. It says that with only six years, the sale counts as a very strong protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחאה is a protest that warns the person in possession to guard his proof of purchase. Here the גמרא says that selling the land to someone else is the clearest protest there can be. So the person in possession should have kept his document, and he loses if he cannot produce it.

keyTerms.meaning: A protest that the owner makes against someone using his land, so that person knows to keep his proof
Six (years)
There is nothing greater than this

steps.whatToRemember: An act like selling the land to someone else counts as the strongest kind of מחאה.

phrases.english: But six [years] —
you have no greater protest than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שֵׁית אֵין לְךָ מֶחָאָה גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the case from the earlier part of the דף.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With only six years, the sale to another person is the strongest possible מחאה.

steps.title: Two people each say the field came from their ancestors
steps.stepSummary: A new case: each side says the field is his inheritance. One brings witnesses that it was his ancestors'. The other brings witnesses that he has used it for the years of חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one says, 'It was my ancestors',' and that one says, 'It was my ancestors'.' This one brings witnesses that it was his ancestors', and that one brings witnesses that he used it for the years of חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new court case. It is setting up the question that רבה and אביי will argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has witnesses, but about different things. The first side's witnesses say the field once belonged to his family. The person in possession has witnesses only that he used it for three years, and he claims an inheritance that the first witnesses contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: It belonged to my ancestors, so I inherited it
Witnesses
He used it (literally: 'ate it'), meaning he took the field's produce
The years needed to set up a claim of ownership (three years)

phrases.english: This one says: 'It belonged to my ancestors,'
and that one says: 'It belonged to my ancestors';
this one brought witnesses that it was his ancestors',
and that one brought witnesses
that he used it for the years of חזקה —
phrases.notes: חזקה years means three years of using the field. That normally lets the one holding it keep it if he says he bought it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר שֶׁל אֲבוֹתַי וְזֶה אוֹמֵר שֶׁל אֲבוֹתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new case, separate from the protest discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: competing inheritance claims, with witnesses to ancestry on one side and witnesses to three years of use on the other.

steps.title: רבה: the one in possession wins, because why would he lie?
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules for the person in possession. He could have said 'I bought it from you,' which would have won, so we believe his weaker claim too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Why would he lie? If he wanted, he could have said to him, 'I bought it from you and used it for the years of חזקה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his ruling on the case. He says the person in possession keeps the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מה לו לשקר means this: if a person could have won with a better claim, we trust the claim he actually made. The person in possession has three years of use, so 'I bought it from you' would have won. Therefore רבה believes him when he says 'my ancestors'.'

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the first ruling here
Why would he lie? We trust a claim when a better claim was available to him
I bought it from you

steps.whyThisMatters: מה לי לשקר is a basic tool in דיני ממונות, and this case tests how far it reaches.

phrases.english: Rabba said: Why would he lie?
If he wanted, he could have said to him:
'I bought it from you'
'and I used it for the years of חזקה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case set up in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person in possession keeps the field, based on מה לו לשקר.

steps.title: אביי: 'Why would he lie' does not work against witnesses
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects. We do not use מה לי לשקר when witnesses contradict the claim the person actually made.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: We do not say 'why would I lie' where there are witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's ruling. He says the reasoning fails because there are witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses say the field belonged to the other man's ancestors, so 'my ancestors'' is shown to be false. מה לי לשקר can support a claim that has no proof against it. It cannot save a claim that witnesses have already disproven.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who challenges רבה here
Where there are witnesses (against the claim)
We do not say (this rule)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not denying the possessor's three years of use. He is saying that his actual claim, 'my ancestors',' is contradicted by witnesses. Because of that, the better claim he could have made does not help him.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
'Why would I lie' in a place where there are witnesses —
we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי מָה לִי לְשַׁקֵּר בִּמְקוֹם עֵדִים לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's use of מה לו לשקר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the person in possession wins because of מה לו לשקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מה לי לשקר cannot support a claim that witnesses directly contradict, and here the witnesses say the field was the other side's ancestors'.

steps.title: The one in possession changes his claim: 'I bought it from you'
steps.stepSummary: The person in possession now admits the field was the other man's ancestors'. He says he bought it, and that 'my ancestors'' only meant he relies on it as if it were inherited.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said to him: Yes, it was your ancestors', and I bought it from you. When I told you 'my ancestors',' I meant that I rely on it as if it were my ancestors'.
steps.whatsHappening: The person in possession changes his story and explains away his first words. The גמרא is setting up the next question: can he change his claim like this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: His new claim fits the witnesses, since the field was the other man's ancestors'. It also matches his three years of use, which normally wins with a claim of purchase. He reads his earlier words, 'my ancestors',' as just a way of saying he is as secure in the field as if he had inherited it.

keyTerms.meaning: He then went back and said to him
Yes
I rely on it (I feel secure in owning it)
As if it were my ancestors'

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the classic question of טוען וחוזר וטוען: can a person in court change his claim and explain away what he said before?

phrases.english: He then said to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person who has been using the field, now answering the other side.

phrases.english: 'Yes, it was your ancestors' —
'and I bought it from you;'
'and that which I told you, that it was my ancestors','
'[I meant] that I rely on it as if it were my ancestors'.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִין דַּאֲבָהָתָךְ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי rejects מה לי לשקר, the case develops: the person in possession revises his claim to one the witnesses do not contradict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case development: the person in possession now claims purchase and reinterprets his earlier 'my ancestors'' claim. This sets up whether a revised claim is accepted.

steps.title: May a person change his claim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a litigant may state one claim and then come back with an adjusted claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a person make a claim and then come back and make a different claim, or can he not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a general question that comes out of the last case. This step sets up the dispute that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man in possession first said 'it was my ancestors''. Then he said 'I bought it'. Before we can rule for him, we need to know whether a person is even allowed to shift his claim after stating it.

keyTerms.meaning: makes a legal claim
and comes back and claims again (an adjusted version)

phrases.english: Does he claim, and come back and claim again,
or does he not claim and come back and claim again?

steps.triggerLanguage: טוֹעֵן וְחוֹזֵר וְטוֹעֵן, אוֹ אֵין טוֹעֵן וְחוֹזֵר וְטוֹעֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the possessor's changed claim from step 5 into a general legal question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a litigant may adjust his claim after he has already stated it.

steps.title: עולא allows it, נהרדעא does not
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that a person may adjust his claim. The חכמי נהרדעא rule that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: he may claim and come back and claim again. The Sages of נהרדעא say: he may not claim and come back and claim again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a מחלוקת between עולא and the חכמי נהרדעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא lets a person go back and fix or explain what he said. The חכמי נהרדעא hold that once a person states his claim, he is stuck with it.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who often traveled between ארץ ישראל and בבל
the Sages of נהרדעא, a city in בבל

phrases.english: Ulla said:
He may claim, and come back and claim again.
The Sages of Neharde'a say:
He may not claim and come back and claim again.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: טוֹעֵן וְחוֹזֵר וְטוֹעֵן. נְהַרְדָּעֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with two opposing views.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא: a claim may be adjusted. נהרדעא: a claim may not be adjusted.

steps.title: Where עולא agrees a claim cannot be changed
steps.stepSummary: עולא admits two exceptions. A person may not switch to a claim that contradicts what he said. He also may not add a claim right after stepping out of court, because someone probably coached him.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא agrees that if he said 'It was my ancestors' and not your ancestors'', he cannot change his claim. He also agrees that if he stood in court and did not make a claim, then went outside, came back and made it, he cannot. Why? Someone taught him that claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the limits of עולא's view. These are two cases where even עולא forbids changing the claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, 'and not your ancestors'' flatly denies any connection to the other side. 'I bought it from you' would directly contradict it, so that is not a clarification. In the second case, the new claim only appeared after a trip outside. That makes it look invented by someone else, not a true explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: and he agrees (concedes in this case)
from outside
taught him (someone coached him)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think עולא lets a person say anything new. He only allows an adjustment that explains the first claim. A claim that contradicts it is not allowed, and neither is one that looks coached.

phrases.english: And Ulla agrees where he said to him:
'It was my ancestors' and not your ancestors''
phrases.notes: By adding 'not your ancestors'', he ruled out ever having gotten it from the other side's family.

phrases.english: that he may not claim and come back and claim again.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵיכָא דַּהֲוָה קָאֵי בֵּי דִינָא וְלָא טְעַן,
phrases.english: And where he was standing in court and did not make the claim,
and he came from outside and made it,
he may not come back and claim.
What is the reason?
Someone taught him his claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows עולא's ruling from step 7 by giving cases where he agrees with נהרדעא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to עולא, a claim cannot be changed if the new claim contradicts the old one, or if it was added right after leaving the court.

steps.title: Where נהרדעא agrees a claim can be changed
steps.stepSummary: The חכמי נהרדעא admit two exceptions. A person may explain that 'my ancestors'' meant his ancestors who bought it from the other side. He may also make a claim in court that he never mentioned outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages of נהרדעא agree that if he said 'It was my ancestors', who bought it from your ancestors', he may come back and claim. They also agree that if he talked about the matter outside and did not make a claim, then came to court and made it, he may. Why? A person tends to reveal his claims only to the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the limits of the נהרדעא view. These are two cases where even they allow the claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'My ancestors' who bought it from yours' does not cancel the first claim. It just fills it in, so it is allowed. Also, keeping quiet about a claim outside court is normal. People save their arguments for בית דין, so it does not look made up.

keyTerms.meaning: who bought it
who spoke about the matter
reveals

phrases.english: And the Sages of Neharde'a agree where he said to him:
'It was my ancestors', who bought it from your ancestors''
that he may come back and claim.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵיכָא דְּאִישְׁתַּעִי מִילֵּי אַבָּרַאי וְלָא טְעַן,
phrases.english: And where he discussed the matter outside and did not make the claim,
and he came to court and made it,
he may come back and claim.
What is the reason?
A person tends not to reveal his claims
except to the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 8 by narrowing the נהרדעא view with cases where they agree with עולא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to נהרדעא, a person may explain his first claim without contradicting it. He may also make a claim in court that he did not mention outside.

steps.title: אמימר of נהרדעא sides with עולא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר, himself from נהרדעא, holds that a person may adjust his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: I am from נהרדעא, yet I hold that a person may claim and come back and claim again.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא from נהרדעא breaks with his own city's view and agrees with עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It carries weight that someone from the נהרדעא school sides against it. This sets up the final הלכה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא from נהרדעא
I hold (this is my view)

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
I am from Neharde'a myself,
and yet I hold that he may claim, and come back and claim again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an authority supporting עולא's side of the מחלוקת from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A litigant may adjust his claim.

steps.title: The final ruling: a claim may be adjusted
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that a person may claim and come back and claim again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: he may claim and come back and claim again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה, following עולא and אמימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A litigant may explain or adjust his claim, within the limits set out in step 8. So the man in step 5 may change 'my ancestors'' to 'I bought it'.

keyTerms.meaning: and the הלכה is

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows עולא: a person may adjust his claim. He still may not switch to a claim that contradicts what he said, or bring a claim that looks coached right after leaving court.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the ruling that lets the man holding the field explain his first words and still keep his חזקה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
He may claim, and come back and claim again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns אמימר's support for עולא into the binding הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that a litigant may adjust his claim, with the exceptions that עולא himself agrees to.

steps.title: A new case: two claims of inherited land
steps.stepSummary: Each side says the land came from his ancestors. One has witnesses to ancestral ownership plus years of use. The other has witnesses only to years of use.
steps.simpleTranslation: One person says, 'It belonged to my ancestors,' and the other says, 'It belonged to my ancestors.' The first brings witnesses that it belonged to his ancestors and that he used it for the years of חזקה. The second brings witnesses only that he used it for the years of חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out a new case about a land dispute. It is setting up the ruling of רב נחמן that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides make the same claim, so the difference lies in their evidence. The first side proves two things: his ancestors owned the land, and he used it. The second side proves only that he used it. The question is how to weigh these two sets of witnesses against each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
The years of use (three years) that establish a claim of ownership
His ancestors

phrases.english: This one says: It belonged to my ancestors,
and that one says: It belonged to my ancestors;
this one brought witnesses that it was his ancestors'
and that he used it for the years of חזקה,
and that one brought witnesses
that he used it for the years of חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: שֶׁל אֲבוֹתַי, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: שֶׁל אֲבוֹתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case after the הלכה about adjusting claims was decided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case: equal claims, with unequal evidence.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules that the land goes to the ancestral owner
steps.stepSummary: The two testimonies about use cancel each other out, which leaves only the testimony about the ancestors, so the land goes to the first side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Set one testimony about use against the other testimony about use, and establish the land as belonging to the ancestors' line.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן decides the case. The two claims of using the land cancel out, so the first side wins because of his ancestors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has witnesses to three years of use, so neither proof about use outweighs the other. Once those cancel out, the only evidence left is the first side's proof that his ancestors owned the land. That proof decides the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up, establish
Against, opposite
Using the land and taking its produce
The presumed ownership of the ancestors

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Set the using against the using,
phrases.notes: The two sets of witnesses about using the land cancel each other out.

phrases.english: and establish the land in the ownership of the ancestors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אוֹקִי אֲכִילָה לְבַהֲדֵי אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case set out in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The testimonies about use cancel out, and the land goes to the side whose ancestors are proven to have owned it.

steps.title: רבא objects that the first side's witnesses were contradicted
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the first side's witnesses were contradicted, so their testimony should not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But this testimony has been contradicted!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן. He says the first side's witnesses were contradicted, so their whole testimony should be thrown out, including the part about the ancestors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side's witnesses testified about two things: the ancestors and the use. Their testimony about use clashes with the second side's witnesses. רבא holds that once testimony is contradicted in one part, it cannot be relied on for the other part either.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that is contradicted by other witnesses

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But this is contradicted testimony!
phrases.notes: He means the first side's witnesses. The other witnesses say the second side used the land during those same years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: הָא עֵדוּת מוּכְחֶשֶׁת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reliance on the first side's testimony about the ancestors.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same witnesses were contradicted about the use, so all of their testimony, including the part about the ancestors, should be thrown out.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins to answer: the contradiction was only about use
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן concedes that the witnesses were contradicted about the use, and he begins to argue that this does not cancel the rest of their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Granted that it was contradicted about the using of the land,
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts his answer to רבא. He admits one point, and his main argument continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן agrees that the testimony about use was contradicted. The word 'granted' signals that a 'but' is coming: the contradiction about use does not touch the testimony about the ancestors.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, even though (admits one point before arguing another)
Was contradicted

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. The rest of רב נחמן's answer continues right after this line.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא.

phrases.english: Granted that it was contradicted about the using of it,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the contradiction to one part of the testimony
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא assumed that a contradiction in one part ruins the entire testimony.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן concedes the contradiction about use and begins arguing that the testimony about the ancestors still stands. His argument continues in the next part of the גמרא.
